speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To understand what is causing these symptoms, how many days have you been experiencing them?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease.

I have gathered enough information from your history regarding the rash pattern and fever onset to make this determination. While the symptoms of fever, rash, and rhinorrhea can suggest viral exanthems like measles or roseola, the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area in an 11-year-old is highly characteristic of Kawasaki Disease, although it is more common in younger children. I would like to confirm if you have noticed any swelling in your hands or feet, redness of the eyes (conjunctivitis), or if your tongue looks red and strawberry-like.
